title: Serbian Football Star Files Police Complaint Over Former Chief's Intimidation Plot
content:
Serbian football star Nemanja Matić has filed a criminal complaint against Slaviša Kokeza, the former president of the Football Association of Serbia (FSS), following revelations that the official plotted to threaten and intimidate him.

Matić confirmed to OCCRP’s Serbian partner KRIK that he filed the complaint for "endangering safety" two weeks ago at a police station in his hometown of Ub. He declined to comment further on the case.

The move comes after a June 30 investigation by OCCRP and KRIK revealed that Kokeza used the encrypted Sky ECC app to discuss hiring mafia figures to assault a group of high-profile players. The targets included Matić, Danko Lazović, and Manchester United legend Nemanja Vidić, who had publicly criticized Kokeza's leadership.

According to the leaked 2020 messages, Kokeza used mob-style language and asked contacts to send people to intimidate the players' inner circles.

"Right now I realistically need the most help to eliminate Vidić, [Danko] Lazović, and Matić," he told one interlocutor.

title: On This Nearly Deserted Alaska Island, You Pay to Keep Hundreds of Empty Buildings Wired for Internet
content:
On an island in the Bering Sea 1,200 miles from Anchorage, Alaska, sits an abandoned house on an abandoned Navy base. There is no furniture, and the wind blows through broken windows. The last people to live here moved away long ago. Yet a bright orange pipe with a black fiber-optic cable inside runs from the outer wall down into the surrounding soil.  

The cable was installed to connect the home to the internet after the base closed. It costs more than $340,000 per year to provide this building and hundreds of others — all but a few of them empty — with internet access no one says they use. 

The money being wasted is yours. 

It comes from a fee added to nearly every American’s phone bill as part of a Federal Communications Commission subsidy program intended to bring fast, affordable internet to remote towns.

Alaskans pay the most for phone and internet but get the slowest service. Please fill out our quick survey to share how much it costs you to get online and what you think of the service.

title: ‘Manchesterism’ is bigger than Andy Burnham
content:
Walk along Manchester’s Oxford Road on a weekday morning and it is difficult not to notice the northern English city’s confidence.

Home to two universities, major NHS hospitals and world-leading research institutions, the Oxford Road Corridor is underpinned by a partnership that brings together universities, public services, businesses and local government around a shared vision for place.

The northern English city of Manchester has played a critical role in the development of Andy Burnham’s political and social outlook. This series considers what some have dubbed Manchesterism and what it might mean for the future of the UK.

Yet only a few miles away, many neighbourhoods continue to experience some of England’s deepest health, economic and social inequalities. Modern Manchester is both one of Britain’s great urban success stories and a reminder that growth alone does not guarantee prosperity for everyone.

Since Andy Burnham became the first elected Mayor of Greater Manchester in 2017, the UK has had five prime ministers: Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, Rishi Sunak and Keir Starmer. Burnham remained in post throughout.

title: Feminist Metascience, Feminist Open Science? Pain Points and Possibilities - Christin L. Munsch, Daisy Verduzco Reyes, 2026
content: Abstract:  This introduction brings feminist scholarship into conversation with metascience and open science. Drawing on feminist epistemology, we argue scientific reform is not a neutral technical project. Rather, practices intended to improve rigor, transparency, and accessibility may also expose marginalized scholars and research participants to harm, reproduce inequality, and facilitate hostile scrutiny, particularly in the current political environment. These tensions point to the need for feminist metascience and feminist open science. We define feminist metascience as the study of how gender and intersecting relations of power shape the production, evaluation, circulation, and correction of scientific knowledge, and we define feminist open science as an approach to transparency that remains attentive to care, protection, and risk. We offer these definitions and the articles in this special issue as a starting point for larger conversations about how feminist scholarship might contribute to emerging debates over scientific reform.

title: The European Parliament’s answer to its AI worries: More AI
content:
The institution is opening its doors to models from OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic and Mistral as it tries to bring lawmakers’ growing use of the technology under control.

By MAX GRIERA
in Brussels

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

As MEPs and their assistants increasingly turn to artificial intelligence to draft speeches, parliamentary questions and even amendments, the European Parliament is seeking to bring that use under control with an officially sanctioned platform of its own.

The internal platform, known as EPGenAI Hub, will give lawmakers and staff access to models from Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and France’s Mistral, offering what Parliament hopes will be a safer alternative to the public AI tools already being used for legislative work. The new platform is currently being tested and could begin rolling out as early as September, according to two people familiar with the plans, granted anonymity to discuss the internal strategy.

title: UK Brings New Trafficking Charges Against Tate Brothers
content:
Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service has brought 38 additional charges against social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate, including rape and trafficking for sexual exploitation, and requested their extradition from the United States.

The brothers were arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service on Saturday, July 18, according to a ⁠CPS statement published the following day. British prosecutors said the new charges concern four additional alleged victims and bring the total number of alleged victims in the U.K. case to seven.

Andrew Tate, 39, faces seven additional rape counts, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, and three counts of assault causing actual bodily harm. He also faces 19 additional charges involving indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Tristan Tate, 38, faces two rape counts, one count of sexual assault, and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.

title: Eight lifesaving ways to improve wildfire risk management
content:
As the flames advanced towards the village of Bédar, in the Almería province of Andalusia, the mayor gave a desperate order to ring the church bells to warn residents. It was not enough. The July 9 Los Gallardos fire, which claimed 13 lives and burnt 7,000 hectares, was Spain’s third deadliest on record.

Most of the victims were retired foreigners living in isolated homes, who died trapped in their vehicles or fleeing on foot along dead-end paths in a landscape dominated by scrubland and rugged terrain, most of which is difficult to access.

High temperatures and extremely dry weather turn scrub, grasslands and bushes into highly flammable fuel. This, combined with complex terrain that makes fire spread faster and unpredictably, poses an enormous challenge for firefighting efforts.

Andalusian legislation requires local emergency plans for forest fires in high-risk areas, and self-protection plans for detached buildings and housing estates. However, there is a widespread problem with compliance and implementation of these measures.

title: Russian Security Service Planned AI Tool to Track Media
content:
Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) had been developing an artificial intelligence system designed to merge public media monitoring with restricted databases to help officers search for information about people and events, according to an investigation by OCCRP partner IStories. 

The project was never delivered, but leaked documents show how the FSB planned to use Artificial Intelligence technology developed by U.S. companies in its intelligence gathering operations.   

The documents indicate that a little-known technology company in Kazan called Micord worked on the system, named PAUK (spider) — a Russian acronym for “Portal for Analytics and Usage of Contents.” The internal documents were obtained after hackers breached Micord’s infrastructure in December 2025 and passed the material to the rights group Idite Lesom, which shared it with IStories.

The same leak was used in earlier IStories investigations into Russia’s digital military registry and other classified Defense Ministry systems.

title: Andy Burnham becomes prime minister after Keir Starmer leaves Downing Street for the last time
content:
After being named leader of the Labour party, Andy Burnham has officially become prime minister of the UK. That many people considered this day an inevitability doesn’t make it any less momentous.

Six years ago, Starmer inherited a Labour party that had failed to win four general elections and was battling a tarnished reputation. In the month he took over as leader, Labour were polling at 29%, 22 points behind Boris Johnson’s Conservative party. Starmer was described as “ruthless”, which he occasionally admitted himself, in turning the party around. He expelled those associated with anti-semitism or who disavowed Labour and spent four years preparing to fight a winning electoral campaign.

The scandals and changes in leadership for the then-governing Conservative party certainly helped Starmer. Labour became more popular than the Tories in November 2021 and held that lead until the July 2024 general election. Starmer looked to persuade voters by promising “national renewal” and a principle of “country first, party second”.

title: DIDAYS 2026 Hamburg
content:
Der CCC Hansestadt Hamburg und die Wau Holland Stiftung veranstalten vom 2. bis 4. Oktober zusammen mit Hamburger Stadtteilinitiativen, Maker- und Hackerspaces und weiteren zivilgesellschaftlichen Organisationen aus der Region die ersten Digital Independence Days in Hamburg. Euch erwartet ein Programm rund um digitale Unabhängigkeit: Messenger, Office-Programm, oder die eigene Cloud.

tl;dr: Vom 2.–4.10.2026 gibt’s drei Tage DIDAYS im Kultur Palast Harburg. Alle Infos unter didays.de

Im Dezember 2025 wurde die Initiative Digital Independence Day ins Leben gerufen, um allen Menschen Möglichkeiten zu zeigen, sich von Big Tech unabhängig zu machen: Bessere Messenger, bessere Office-Software, unabhängige Clouds. In über 100 Städten in Deutschland und darüber hinaus gibt es regelmäßig zum ersten Sonntag im Monat Veranstaltungen mit Vorträgen, Workshops und Austauschformaten. Und auf DIDAY.org gibt es viele Informationen, wie man selbst den Wechsel zu offeneren Alternativen hinbekommen kann.

Das Ziel ist es, euch mehr Kompetenz und Mündigkeit im Umgang mit moderner Technik zu vermitteln.

title: Could AI be conscious?
content:
Experts believe it’s at least possible. We urgently need a plan to navigate the ethical implications

In January, the AI company Anthropic published a new constitution for Claude, its most advanced large language model (LLM), which contained the comment: “We are caught in a difficult position where we neither want to overstate the likelihood of Claude’s moral patienthood nor dismiss it out of hand.” A month later, Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei went on a podcast and said his company couldn’t rule out the possibility that Claude was conscious. Philosopher David Chalmers, who coined the phrase “the hard problem of consciousness”, has said there is a significant chance of conscious LLMs within a decade. And what about Claude itself? When asked during testing to estimate the probability that it is a moral patient, meaning that its wellbeing matters in its own right, it gave numbers ranging from 5% to 40% and stressed how uncertain it was.
snippet: Experts believe it’s at least possible. We urgently need a plan to navigate the ethical implications

title: Trump pushes UN ‘free speech’ declaration in veiled attack on EU tech regulation
content:
BRUSSELS — The Trump administration will use the upcoming U.N. General Assembly to push a global “freedom of expression” declaration that European lawmakers say is a not-so-subtle dig at the bloc’s tech regulation.

POLITICO has obtained a draft of the joint declaration that the U.S. has begun circulating among countries in the hope that it will be signed by heads of government at an event on the sidelines of the annual United Nations meeting in September.

The version of the document seen by POLITICO denounces “new laws” and “regulatory frameworks” that it says endanger free speech around the globe in “historically democratic countries.”

The White House and Republican party allies have repeatedly attacked rules in several jurisdictions that govern online platforms, notably in the European Union, alleging that they amount to censorship. Most memorably, freshly elected U.S. Vice President JD Vance said in February 2025 that the biggest threat to Europe wasn’t Russia or China but its own actions against free speech.

title: Full article: Cross-publisher agreement on the defining principles of plain language summaries of publications (PLSPs)
content: Abstract: Introduced in 2020, plain language summaries of publications (PLSPs) are standalone articles that aim to expand the reach of scientific findings to non-specialist audiences using plain language and meaningful visuals. Despite increased publication, there is no agreed cross-publisher definition of PLSPs, resulting in inconsistent terminology, formatting, peer-review processes, and metadata that hinder indexing and discoverability in bibliographic databases such as PubMed and Europe PMC. In February 2024, the multistakeholder collaboration Open Pharma launched an initiative to review existing standards and practices related to the publication of PLSPs. After identifying three publishers offering standalone PLSPs – Becaris Publishing, Sage, and Taylor & Francis – representatives from each formed a steering committee to define PLSPs and agree on principles that differentiate them from other publishing formats. title: Cuba: Freedom House Welcomes Release of Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara, Calls for Release of Other Political Prisoners
content:
WASHINGTON—Cuban authorities have released political prisoner Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara. Otero Alcántara is an award-winning artist and activist who cofounded the San Isidro Movement to protest the Cuban regime’s increasing censorship of free expression. On July 11, 2021—the start of the historic J11 protests—he was arrested and had been detained since. He has been called “The Cuban Artist the Regime Fears Most."

Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House, issued the following statement:  

“Freedom House welcomes the release of Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara. We commend the Trump administration, other democratic governments, and Cuban civil society for maintaining pressure on the regime, exposing the extent of its abuses, and championing the Cuban people’s aspirations for freedom. That freedom is closer than ever. We will continue to advocate for the more than 1,300 political prisoners still detained in Cuba for speaking out against decades of repression and corruption.”

title: Mandela Day: CIVICUS calls on the public to spend 67 minutes standing with jailed human rights defenders
content:
Johannesburg, South Africa — As the world marks Nelson Mandela Day, CIVICUS is calling on people everywhere to dedicate 67 minutes to solidarity and action for imprisoned human rights defenders through the #StandAsMyWitness campaign.

The number honours the 67 years Nelson Mandela devoted to the struggle for freedom, equality and human rights. While taking action through the campaign takes only a few minutes, the 67-minute call reflects the Mandela Day tradition of giving time in service of justice, dignity and humanity. A small act of solidarity today can contribute to a lasting impact for human rights defenders and the communities they serve.

Launched on Nelson Mandela Day in 2020, Stand As My Witness (SAMW) draws inspiration from Mandela’s legacy and the enduring importance of solidarity with those who are persecuted for defending rights and freedoms. The campaign shines a spotlight on human rights defenders who have been jailed for speaking truth to power and mobilises global support for their release.

title: How a Man Once Ordered to Pay Libel Damages Helped Launch an Investigation Into Islamic Private Schools
content:
Nearly a decade ago, a British court ordered a man named Sam Westrop to pay the equivalent of more than $173,000 in libel damages after he published an article on his website calling the founder of a London-based Islamic TV channel a “convicted terrorist.”

Westrop eventually admitted the underlying evidence for the claim was not reliable, according to court filings, and corrected the story on his website.

“There simply was no evidence to support the allegation of terrorism,” the judge in the case wrote.

Years after that ruling, Westrop made similar claims about a group of Islamic private schools in Texas that had applied to the state’s new voucher program. He alleged the school leaders had connections to Islamic extremist or terrorist groups, such as Hamas. Westrop shared his research as early as last fall with the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, which oversees the voucher program that awards eligible families taxpayer dollars for private education or homeschooling.

title: Remaining active: We provided feedback for various European Commission consultations
content:

The initiative unites most of the former project partners and brings in further parties from the research and tech domain. The goal is not only to continue with various research projects surrounding the OWI, but to further promote the need for a public-private web data infrastructure for Europe. With this mission in mind, we have provided feedback to various EC consultations in the past months.

title: Destination of Sustainable Cultural Tourism Awards 2026: Finalists announced
content:
The finalists of the Destination of Sustainable Cultural Tourism Awards 2026, recognising outstanding initiatives that demonstrate excellence in sustainable, smart, resilient and regenerative cultural tourism across Europe, were announced on 1 July. The awards are organised by ECTN in partnership with Europa Nostra, the European Travel Commission and NECSTour, with support of the INSPIRES SMP-COSME Project, Europeana, the Creative Tourism Network and ENAT.

This year’s finalists compete in six categories aligned with the key themes of the 19th ECTN Conference for Cultural Tourism, which will take place on 23-26 September 2026 on Skiathos Island, Greece, under the theme:

“Sustainable Tourism Strategy and Culture Compass for Europe: Synergies for Regenerative, Smart and Resilient Cultural Tourism.”

The finalists represent destinations, tourism organisations and cultural heritage initiatives from across Europe, showcasing innovative projects that strengthen local communities, preserve and promote cultural heritage, enhance visitor experiences through digital innovation, encourage active and accessible tourism, and advance regenerative approaches to destination development.

title: Keeping Knowledge Accessible Starts Here: Subscribe to the Empowering Libraries Newsletter.
content:
Every day, information professionals at libraries, archives, museums and research organizations all over the world work to ensure that knowledge remains available for future generations. From preserving websites before they disappear to digitizing books, safeguarding government information, and expanding access to cultural heritage, there’s always something happening behind the scenes.

Internet Archive’s Empowering Libraries newsletter brings those stories directly to your inbox.

Subscribe today and receive updates—every two weeks or so—on:

  • The Wayback Machine and web preservation;
  • Democracy’s Library and efforts to preserve public information;
  • Digital preservation projects from around the world;
  • Open Library and expanding access to books;
  • New tools, collections, and research resources;
  • Upcoming events, webinars, and opportunities to participate;
  • Stories from librarians, archivists, and others working to build a more accessible future for knowledge.

    • What’s inside? Check out a recent issue.

title: New Online at the Library of Congress: July 2026
content:
The Library of Congress holds the world’s preeminent body of primary-source materials for the study of the life and work of George and Ira Gershwin, providing a nearly comprehensive record of their music and lyrics, as well as correspondence, photographs, business and financial papers, publicity materials, and press accounts.

This new digital collection primarily features their music (piano-vocal scores, orchestrations, and sketches) and handwritten lyric sheets and librettos. There are also manuscripts, lyric sheets, published sheet music, both concert and theater programs, and at least one self-portrait oil painting of Ira Gershwin smoking a cigarette. What other treasures can you find?

Community Collections Grants from the American Folklife Center supported contemporary cultural field research from 2022-2024. Read more about the program on loc.gov.

title: Lock the Web Open: Inside DWeb Camp 2026
content:
Last week, in an ancient forest an hour outside Berlin, more than 500 builders, researchers, archivists, and artists gathered to ask the same question in a hundred different ways: how do we build a web that cannot be switched off, sold, or shut down. Internet Archive Europe helped bring it there.

For the first time in its ten-year history, DWeb Camp left the redwoods of Northern California. This year it landed at Alte Hölle, a former Stasi recreation site now home to a collectivist community, set on 100,000 square metres of forest and meadow in Brandenburg. The event is co-hosted this year by the Internet Archive, the Department of Decentralization, and IAE, which is why our co-founder Julien Masanès and our Programme Manager Beatrice Murch spent the week there rather than reading about it afterwards.

title: State of the World’s Plants and Fungi Symposium Recordings and Report
content:
The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew recently hosted the 2026 State of the World’s Plants and Fungi Symposium. The event brought together experts to focus on the “digitisation of herbarium and fungarium collections, including its applications and implications.”

Local Contexts Strategic Advisor Maui Hudson (Whakatōhea) presented “Acknowledging local contexts: Recognising Indigenous knowledge and provenance as part of the biocultural value of collections” in Session 4, “Tapping into the biocultural wealth of collections.” The session ended with a panel with the presenters.

Watch the presentation recordings and read the symposium report on Kew’s website.

title: Online event: Navigating changes in Welsh democracy with WriteToThem
content: Online event: Navigating changes in Welsh democracy with WriteToThem View this email in your browser Online event Getting the right message to the right place Navigating democracy in Wales with WriteToThem (23rd July: 12-1pm) The democratic map in Wales has changed. Following the 2026 election, people in Wales now have new constituencies for the Senedd with multiple representatives from different parties. WriteToThem exists to solve the problem of who is the right representative to contact. We help people get from their postcode to the right representative: whether that's a councillor, a Member of the Senedd, or a Member of the UK Parliament. In this hour-long event, the mySociety team (and guest speaker Jess Blair from ERS Cymru) will discuss the changing landscape in Wales, and relaunch the service for Wales, walking through what's new, including the new Welsh language version of the service.
